application.name: Hyundai Nishat Motors Website
application.type: Web application (public corporate and automotive sales/service website)
application.description: The Hyundai Nishat Motors website is the official online presence of Hyundai Nishat Motor (Private) Limited, the company that assembles and sells Hyundai vehicles in Pakistan. Customers use it to browse the vehicle line-up and prices, book a vehicle online, check booking status, request a test drive or brochure, book a service appointment, find a dealer and download owner's manuals. It was chosen because it is a live, feature-rich site with many forms and navigation paths, it was not built by the tester, and it serves a large customer base, so its defects have a real impact on users.

environments.device: HP Laptop 15s-fq2xxx (Intel Core i7-1165G7, 8 GB RAM)
HP Laptop 15s-fq2xxx, Chrome DevTools device emulation
HP Laptop 15s-fq2xxx (Intel Core i7-1165G7, 8 GB RAM)

features: Home page: promotional banners, booking pop-up, quick-action links
Find a Car: vehicle catalogue with category filter (All, Sedan, SUV, Electric, Commercial) and starting prices
Vehicle model pages: Elantra, Elantra Hybrid, Sonata, Sonata N Line, Tucson Hybrid, Santa Fe, Palisade Hybrid, IONIQ 5, IONIQ 6, Porter H-100
Service Appointment Request (Book a Service) form
After Sales: warranty conditions, extended warranty, genuine parts, lubricants, engine oil
Hyundai Service: customer promise, dealership facility, free services, periodic maintenance charts, owner's manual
About Us: overview, corporate message, philosophy
Footer: legal disclaimer, cookie policy, sitemap, social media links

custom_techniques: Desktop–Mobile Parity Check: open the same page and menu on desktop and in mobile view side by side, and compare every item, link target and label. Any difference is a candidate bug (found BUG-001 and BUG-005).

bugs.title: Mobile menu "Appointment Form" link opens the Owner's Manual page instead of the service booking form
bugs.technique: Navigation Testing, Mobile Device Testing, Responsive Design Testing
bugs.description: On mobile, the only link under "Service Appointment Request" is "Appointment Form", but it leads to the Owner's Manual page. Mobile users cannot reach the service booking form from the menu.
bugs.preconditions: Website opened at a mobile screen width
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com on a phone, or in Chrome DevTools device mode (F12, then Ctrl+Shift+M)
Tap the menu icon (☰) and expand After Sales
Under "Service Appointment Request", tap "Appointment Form"
bugs.expected: The service appointment booking form opens (hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/), as the desktop menu's "Service Appointment" link does.
bugs.actual: The Owner's Manual page (hyundai-nishat.com/owners-manual/) opens. No path in the mobile menu leads to the booking form.
bugs.oracle: The link label and its section heading promise an appointment form. The desktop menu's equivalent link opens the booking form, so the same menu item behaves differently by device: an inconsistency oracle. It blocks a core user task (booking a service) for mobile users.

bugs.title: Spelling error "Extented Warranty" in the After Sales menu
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, GUI Testing, Static Testing (Reviews), Cross-Browser Testing
bugs.description: The After Sales menu lists the warranty page as "Extented Warranty". The page it opens is titled "Extended Warranty". Reproduced in Microsoft Edge (ENV-3).
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Hover over or click After Sales in the main menu
Read the items under Warranty
bugs.expected: The menu item reads "Extended Warranty".
bugs.actual: The menu item reads "Extented Warranty", on both desktop and mobile menus.
bugs.oracle: Standard English spelling, and consistency with the destination page, whose heading and breadcrumb both say "Extended Warranty".

bugs.title: Developer's personal email address exposed in the home page source code
bugs.module: Home page – page source (Instagram feed plugin)
bugs.technique: Sensitive Data Exposure Testing, Security Testing, Grey-Box Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The home page HTML includes the Instagram-feed plugin's settings, which contain "mail_to_alert":"umair.munir@crewlogix.com": a named individual's address at a third-party development company.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Press Ctrl+U to view the page source
Press Ctrl+F and search for mail_to_alert
bugs.expected: No personal or developer email addresses appear in public page source; plugin alert settings stay server-side or use a company address.
bugs.actual: The source shows "mail_to_alert":"umair.munir@crewlogix.com" (line 1857 in the page source).
bugs.oracle: OWASP guidance on sensitive data exposure: internal contact details in public code can be harvested for spam and phishing, and reveal the site's vendor. A production site for Hyundai Nishat should not publish a contractor employee's email address.

bugs.title: Open mobile menu does not cover the page: content shows through and overlaps "Hyundai Promise"
bugs.technique: Responsive Design Testing, Mobile Device Testing, Layout and Alignment Testing, GUI Testing
bugs.description: When the mobile menu is expanded, its panel ends before the page content. A car image from the page underneath overlaps the last menu item, "Hyundai Promise".
bugs.preconditions: Website opened at a mobile screen width
steps: Open any page (for example Owner's Manual) at a mobile width
Tap the menu icon (☰)
Expand After Sales and scroll to the bottom of the menu
bugs.expected: The open menu sits on a solid background above all page content, and every menu item is fully readable and tappable.
bugs.actual: The "Hyundai Promise" item is partly covered by a car image from the page below, and page content continues directly under the menu.
bugs.oracle: Usability heuristic: an open navigation menu must be fully visible and usable. The desktop menu has a solid panel, so the mobile behaviour is inconsistent.

bugs.title: "Find a Dealer" is missing from the mobile menu
bugs.technique: Mobile Device Testing, Navigation Testing, Cross-Platform / OS Compatibility Testing, Checklist-Based Testing
bugs.description: The desktop main menu has seven items, including Find a Dealer. The mobile menu shows only six: Find a Car, After Sales, Hyundai Pakistan, Press Release, Hyundai Easy Own and Hyundai Promise.
bugs.preconditions: Website opened at a mobile screen width
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com on desktop and note the main menu items
Switch to a mobile width and tap the menu icon (☰)
Compare the two lists
bugs.expected: The mobile menu offers the same main sections as desktop, including Find a Dealer.
bugs.actual: Find a Dealer does not appear in the mobile menu.
bugs.oracle: Consistency oracle: the desktop menu is the specification of the site's main sections. Finding a dealer is a key task for car buyers, and many of them browse on phones.

bugs.title: Extended Warranty breadcrumb skips the "After Sales" level
bugs.technique: Navigation Testing, Checklist-Based Testing, GUI Testing
bugs.description: The Extended Warranty page's breadcrumb reads "Home > Extended Warranty", although the page sits under After Sales in the menu.
steps: Open After Sales > Extended Warranty
Read the breadcrumb under the menu
Open After Sales > Owner's Manual and compare its breadcrumb
bugs.expected: Home > After Sales > Extended Warranty
bugs.actual: Home > Extended Warranty
bugs.oracle: Consistency oracle: Owner's Manual, also under After Sales, shows "Home > After Sales > Owner's Manual". Breadcrumbs should reflect the site hierarchy.

bugs.title: Stray backtick instead of an apostrophe in "HNMPL ` s warranty"
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The opening paragraph of the Extended Warranty page reads "backed by HNMPL ` s warranty coverage", with a backtick surrounded by spaces.
steps: Open After Sales > Extended Warranty
Read the first bold paragraph below the warranty badge
bugs.expected: "backed by HNMPL's warranty coverage"
bugs.actual: "backed by HNMPL ` s warranty coverage"
bugs.oracle: Standard English punctuation for the possessive. The error is in the page's main promotional sentence, so it affects the brand's credibility.

bugs.title: Missing space in "up to125,000 KM"
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The last benefit bullet on the Extended Warranty page reads "Offers up to125,000 KM / 5 Years Warranty".
steps: Open After Sales > Extended Warranty
Read the bullet list under "Enjoy peace of mind with Hyundai Extended Warranty"
bugs.expected: "Offers up to 125,000 KM / 5 Years Warranty"
bugs.actual: "Offers up to125,000 KM / 5 Years Warranty"
bugs.oracle: Standard typography: a space separates a word from the number that follows it.

bugs.title: Vehicle line-up differs between the home page and the Owner's Manual page
bugs.module: Home page vehicles vs Owner's Manual
bugs.technique: Data Integrity Testing, Business Rule Testing, Exploratory Testing
bugs.description: The home page lists "SANTA FE HYBRID" and no plain Tucson. The Owner's Manual page lists "SANTA FE" (not hybrid) and adds a separate "TUCSON". The two pages disagree on which models Hyundai Nishat offers.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com and scroll to the Vehicles section
Note the model names
Open After Sales > Owner's Manual and compare the model names
bugs.expected: Both pages list the same models with the same names, or the Owner's Manual clearly marks discontinued models.
bugs.actual: Home: Elantra 1.6 Special Edition, Elantra Hybrid, Sonata, Sonata N Line, Tucson Hybrid, Santa Fe Hybrid, Palisade Hybrid, IONIQ 5, IONIQ 6, Porter H-100 (10 models). Owner's Manual: adds "TUCSON" and names "SANTA FE" instead of "SANTA FE HYBRID" (11 models).
bugs.oracle: Data integrity oracle: the same product data should match across pages. A Santa Fe Hybrid owner may download the wrong manual, and customers get conflicting information about which models are sold.

bugs.title: "Trending around you" tiles cut their captions off mid-sentence
bugs.technique: GUI Testing, Layout and Alignment Testing, Content and Spelling Testing
bugs.description: Captions at the bottom of the promotional tiles are truncated, for example "Bring home the SANTA FE Hybrid and" and "Choose the TUCSON Hybrid and", with no ellipsis or way to read the rest.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Scroll to "Trending around you"
Read the captions at the bottom of the second and third tiles
bugs.expected: Each caption is shown in full, or ends with an ellipsis and the tile links to the full offer.
bugs.actual: Captions stop mid-sentence and the rest of the text is hidden.
bugs.oracle: Usability heuristic: text must not be clipped without an indication. The captions carry the offer details, so users miss the key information.

bugs.title: Home page banner still promotes the "TUCSON Hybrid 2025"
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Business Rule Testing, Exploratory Testing
bugs.description: The main home page carousel shows "The all-new Hyundai TUCSON Hybrid 2025" in November 2026.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Watch the hero carousel until the TUCSON Hybrid slide appears
bugs.expected: Banners promote current model-year vehicles, or omit the year.
bugs.actual: The slide calls a 2025 model "all-new" in late 2026.
bugs.oracle: Currency of content: the site footer says "Copyright 2026", and an "all-new" claim for a previous model year is outdated marketing.

bugs.title: Owner's Manual download buttons misaligned in the first row
bugs.technique: Layout and Alignment Testing, GUI Testing, Visual Regression Testing
bugs.description: "ELANTRA 1.6 SPECIAL EDITION" wraps onto two lines, which pushes its Download button lower than the Download buttons of the other three vehicles in the same row.
steps: Open After Sales > Owner's Manual on a 1920×1080 screen
Look at the first row of vehicles
bugs.expected: All Download buttons in a row line up horizontally, whatever the length of the model name.
bugs.actual: The first Download button sits about one line lower than the other three.
bugs.oracle: Visual consistency in a grid layout. Every other row on the page is aligned, so this row is the exception.

bugs.title: Name field accepts digits only ("12345") without any validation error
bugs.technique: Input Validation Testing, Negative Testing, Equivalence Partitioning, Special Character Testing
bugs.description: The required Name field accepts a value made only of numbers. On submit, every other empty field shows an error, but Name shows none, so a booking can carry an invalid customer name.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Type 12345 in the Name field
Leave the other fields empty and click Submit
Look at the message under Name
bugs.expected: An error such as "Please enter a valid name (letters only)" under the Name field.
bugs.actual: No error under Name; the value 12345 is accepted as a name.
bugs.oracle: A personal name belongs to the equivalence class of alphabetic text. Digits-only input is an invalid class and should be rejected, as the form already validates other fields.

bugs.title: Required drop-down fields show no error when left empty
bugs.technique: Required Field Testing, Error Message Testing, Error Handling Testing, Decision Table Testing
bugs.description: Model, Model Name, Service type, City and Dealer name are all marked required (*). When the form is submitted with them empty, text fields show "Please fill out this field" but none of these five drop-downs shows any message.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Leave every field empty (or fill only Name)
Click Submit
Compare the messages under text fields with those under the drop-downs
bugs.expected: Each empty required drop-down shows "Please fill out this field", like the text fields.
bugs.actual: Only a general banner, "One or more fields have an error", appears. The five drop-downs show no message, so the user cannot tell they still need filling.
bugs.oracle: Consistency oracle: the form marks these fields with * and validates other required fields inline. Usability guidance (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification) says the field in error must be identified to the user.

bugs.title: Form section is headed "Salutation" but contains no salutation field
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Usability Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The heading above the booking fields reads "Salutation", which means a title such as Mr or Ms. The section holds contact, vehicle and appointment details and has no salutation field. The Request a Test Drive form uses the same "Salutation" heading above its Vehicle, City and Dealer fields.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Scroll to the start of the form
Read the section heading and the fields below it
bugs.expected: A heading that describes the section, such as "Your details" or "Appointment details", or a real Salutation (Mr/Ms) field.
bugs.actual: The heading "Salutation" sits above fields that have nothing to do with a salutation.
bugs.oracle: Label accuracy: a heading must describe its content. The mismatch suggests a template heading left unchanged.

bugs.title: Grammar error in the page subtitle: "Hyundai provide you with booking service"
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The subtitle under "Book a Service" reads "Hyundai provide you with booking service for your valuable time."
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Read the subtitle under the "Book a Service" heading
bugs.expected: "Hyundai provides you with a booking service to save your valuable time."
bugs.actual: "Hyundai provide you with booking service for your valuable time."
bugs.oracle: English grammar: a singular subject (Hyundai) takes "provides", and "booking service" needs an article.

bugs.title: Unit written as "Odometer (KM's)" with a wrong apostrophe
bugs.technique: Content and Spelling Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The Odometer label and placeholder both read "Odometer (KM's)".
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Find the Odometer field in the form
bugs.expected: "Odometer (km)"
bugs.actual: "Odometer (KM's)" in both the label and the placeholder.
bugs.oracle: SI unit style: the kilometre symbol is "km", and unit symbols take no plural or apostrophe.

bugs.title: Comments field is mandatory for a service booking
bugs.technique: Usability Testing, Business Rule Testing, Required Field Testing
bugs.description: "Comments (max 2,000 characters)" is marked required, and the form cannot be submitted without typing something in it.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Fill every field except Comments
Click Submit
bugs.expected: Comments are optional; a routine service can be booked without writing a note.
bugs.actual: "Please fill out this field" appears under Comments and the booking is blocked.
bugs.oracle: Form usability practice: free-text notes should be optional. Forcing them adds effort and leads to filler text such as "none" in bookings.

bugs.title: VIN field placeholder shows a realistic VIN that looks pre-filled
bugs.technique: Usability Testing, GUI Testing, Error Guessing
bugs.description: The optional VIN number field shows "MALAA02HR4M123456" in grey. It looks like an already-entered value rather than an example.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/ (After Sales > Service Appointment)
Look at the empty VIN number field
bugs.expected: A clearly marked hint, such as "e.g. MALAA02HR4M123456" or "17-character VIN".
bugs.actual: A full, realistic VIN is shown as the placeholder with no "e.g.".
bugs.oracle: Placeholder guidance (Nielsen Norman Group): placeholders that look like real data are mistaken for filled fields. Users may skip it or think the site already knows their car.

bugs.title: Invalid email "abc@" gives a misleading message: "Please enter an email address"
bugs.technique: Error Message Testing, Input Validation Testing, Boundary Value Analysis, Negative Testing
bugs.description: When the Email field contains an incomplete address such as "abc@", the form says "Please enter an email address", as if the field were empty. The message only appears after Submit is clicked, not when the user leaves the field. The same message appears on the Request a Test Drive form.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Type abc@ in the Email field and click into the next field
Click Submit and read the message under Email
bugs.expected: A specific message such as "Please enter a valid email address (e.g. name@example.com)", shown as soon as the user leaves the field.
bugs.actual: No message when leaving the field. After Submit: "Please enter an email address.", although an address was entered.
bugs.oracle: Error-message guidelines (WCAG 3.3.3 Error Suggestion): a message should say what is wrong and how to fix it. "Enter an email address" is wrong for a field that already holds text.

bugs.title: "Model Name" does not depend on "Model": it lists model names and can be chosen while Model is empty
bugs.technique: State Transition Testing, Cause-Effect Graphing, Integration Testing, Decision Table Testing
bugs.description: Model and Model Name should work as a pair (choose a model, then its version). Instead, Model Name repeats a list of models (Elantra, Sonata, Tucson, Porter, Starex, Staria, Santa Fe, Ioniq, Other) and can be filled while Model is still "Select".
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Leave Model on "Select"
Open the Model Name drop-down and pick Staria
bugs.expected: Model Name stays disabled until a Model is chosen, then lists only that model's versions (for example Elantra → 1.6 Special Edition, Hybrid).
bugs.actual: Model Name is enabled with Model empty, offers model names rather than versions, and accepts Staria while Model shows nothing.
bugs.oracle: Dependent-field logic (cause-effect): a child field should only accept values valid for its parent. Two fields asking the same question, with no link, let users send contradictory data.

bugs.title: Model list does not match the current line-up: Palisade missing, Starex and Staria listed
bugs.technique: Data Integrity Testing, Business Rule Testing, Equivalence Partitioning
bugs.description: The service form's model list offers Starex and Staria, which appear nowhere else on the site, and has no Palisade, which is sold on the site (Palisade Hybrid). IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 6 are merged into one "Ioniq" entry.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Open the Model Name drop-down
Compare it with the Vehicles section on the home page
bugs.expected: The list covers every model the dealer services, including all current models such as Palisade Hybrid, with the same names as the rest of the site.
bugs.actual: Palisade is missing; Starex and Staria are listed; IONIQ 5/6 appear only as "Ioniq".
bugs.oracle: Data integrity oracle: the home page and Owner's Manual list Palisade Hybrid, IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 6 as current models. A Palisade owner cannot correctly book a service.

bugs.title: Service appointment time allows any 15-minute slot from 00:00 to 23:45
bugs.technique: Boundary Value Analysis, Business Rule Testing, Date and Time Testing
bugs.description: The time picker offers all 96 slots of the day, including night times such as 03:00, with no link to dealership working hours.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Click the Service appointment time field
Scroll through the offered times
bugs.expected: Only slots within dealership working hours (for example 09:00 to 17:00) can be chosen.
bugs.actual: All 96 slots from 00:00 to 23:45 are offered in 15-minute steps, and night times such as 04:45 and 20:00 are accepted in the field (screenshots cover the whole list).
bugs.oracle: Business rule oracle: service centres do not work at night. Accepting a 03:00 booking creates appointments the dealer cannot honour.

bugs.title: Dealer list is not filtered by the selected City
bugs.technique: Integration Testing, Cause-Effect Graphing, Decision Table Testing
bugs.description: Dealer name shows every dealer in Pakistan (Chakwal, DG Khan, Gujranwala, Islamabad, Karachi, Lahore, Quetta, Sargodha and more) regardless of the City field.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Leave City on "Select City" (or choose a city)
Open the Dealer name drop-down
bugs.expected: Dealer name is disabled until a city is chosen, then lists only that city's dealers.
bugs.actual: All dealers nationwide are listed, so a user can pick a city and a dealer in a different city.
bugs.oracle: Dependent-field logic: the form asks for City first, which only makes sense if it narrows the dealer list. Mismatched city and dealer leads to wrong bookings.

bugs.title: Dealer names do not show their location ("Hyundai-South", "Hyundai-Premium", "Hyundai-Central")
bugs.technique: Usability Testing, Content and Spelling Testing
bugs.description: Many dealers are listed by internal names that give no city or area, for example Hyundai-South, Hyundai-Highway, Hyundai-Central, Hyundai-Premium, Hyundai-Eastern and Hyundai-Metropolitan. Naming is also inconsistent: "Hyundai-City-Store-Karachi" and "Hyundai-City-Store" both appear.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Open the Dealer name drop-down
Read the dealer names
bugs.expected: Each dealer shows its city and area, for example "Hyundai Central – Lahore".
bugs.actual: Hyphenated internal names with no location, and two similar "City-Store" entries.
bugs.oracle: Usability heuristic (match between system and real world): customers choose a dealer by location, which these labels do not give.

bugs.title: Test Drive form also accepts digits only ("12345") as Full Name
bugs.technique: Input Validation Testing, Negative Testing, Equivalence Partitioning, Regression Testing
bugs.description: The same name-validation gap as BUG-013 exists on a second form: Full Name accepts "12345" and shows no error, while other fields are flagged.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Type 12345 in Full Name and abc@ in Email
Click Submit
Look under Full Name
bugs.expected: "Please enter a valid name" under Full Name.
bugs.actual: No error under Full Name.
bugs.oracle: Equivalence partitioning: digits-only is an invalid class for a person's name. Finding the defect on a second form shows it is a site-wide validation gap, not a one-off.

bugs.title: Required "Vehicle" and "Salutation" show no error when empty, although City and Dealer Name do
bugs.technique: Required Field Testing, Error Message Testing, Decision Table Testing
bugs.description: On submit with empty drop-downs, City and Dealer Name show "Please fill out this field", but Vehicle and Salutation, also marked required (*), show nothing.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Leave all drop-downs on "Select"
Fill Full Name and Email with any text
Click Submit
bugs.expected: Every empty required drop-down shows "Please fill out this field".
bugs.actual: Errors appear under City and Dealer Name only; Vehicle and Salutation stay unmarked. Only the general banner hints at a problem.
bugs.oracle: Consistency within the same form: two required drop-downs are validated and two are not. WCAG 3.3.1 requires the field in error to be identified.

bugs.title: Consent text contains an unfilled template blank ("Order**No:……..………") and refers to a Vehicle Sales Order
bugs.technique: Static Testing (Reviews), Content and Spelling Testing, Business Rule Testing
bugs.description: The Terms & Agreement users must accept says data comes "through the Vehicle Sales Order / Retail Customer Order**No:……..…………("the Order Form")". The order-number blank was never filled, and a test-drive request has no sales order. The company name is also written both "(private)" and "(Private)".
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Scroll to "Disclose Personal Data/Information"
Read paragraph 1.2 of Terms & Agreement
bugs.expected: Consent text written for an online test-drive request, with no unfilled blanks and the company name spelled consistently.
bugs.actual: Paragraph 1.2 contains "Order**No:……..…………" copied from a paper sales-order form; the company appears as both "(private)" and "(Private)".
bugs.oracle: Legal text that users consent to must be accurate and complete. Pakistan's data protection practice and general privacy principles require consent to be informed; a template with blanks for another document does not describe this form's processing.

bugs.title: Salutation list offers only Mr., Mrs. and Other: no Ms. or Miss
bugs.technique: Usability Testing, Equivalence Partitioning, Checklist-Based Testing
bugs.description: The required Salutation drop-down lists Mr., Mrs. and Other. Unmarried women, or women who don't use a marital title, have no option except "Other".
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Open the Salutation drop-down
bugs.expected: At least Mr., Mrs., Ms. and Miss (and optionally Dr.).
bugs.actual: Only Mr., Mrs. and Other.
bugs.oracle: Standard form design practice and common salutation sets include Ms./Miss. Equivalence partitioning of users shows a whole group with no matching value.

bugs.title: Page promises a test drive "appointment" but the form has no date or time field
bugs.technique: Use Case Testing, Business Rule Testing, Scenario-Based Testing
bugs.description: The subtitle says "request a test drive appointment", but the form only collects vehicle, city, dealer and contact details. There is no way to choose a preferred date or time.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Read the subtitle under "Request a Test Drive"
Look through the form for a date or time field
bugs.expected: A preferred date and time field, as on the Book a Service form, or wording that says the dealer will call to arrange a time.
bugs.actual: No date or time field; the user cannot say when they want the test drive.
bugs.oracle: Use-case oracle: an appointment needs a time. The site's own Book a Service form asks for date and time, so this form is inconsistent with it.

bugs.title: "Vehicle*" label has no space before the asterisk, unlike every other label
bugs.technique: GUI Testing, Typography and Font Consistency Testing, Visual Regression Testing
bugs.description: The first label reads "Vehicle*", while all other required labels have a space before the asterisk ("City *", "Dealer Name *").
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/request-a-test-drive/ (home page > Request a Test Drive)
Look at the labels on the left of the form
bugs.expected: "Vehicle *", formatted like the other labels.
bugs.actual: "Vehicle*" with no space.
bugs.oracle: Visual consistency: labels in one form should follow the same format.

bugs.title: Reset button has a colour contrast of 1.6:1 and looks disabled
bugs.technique: Accessibility Testing, Colour Contrast Testing, GUI Testing
bugs.description: The Reset button uses white text on a light grey background (#CCCCCC). Measured from the screenshot, the contrast ratio is 1.61:1, far below the 4.5:1 minimum. The button looks greyed out, so users cannot tell it works.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com/book-a-service/
Scroll to the Submit and Reset buttons
Measure the Reset button's text and background colours (e.g. with Chrome DevTools or a contrast checker)
bugs.expected: Button text with at least 4.5:1 contrast, styled as an active secondary button.
bugs.actual: Contrast 1.61:1; the button looks disabled although it is active.
bugs.oracle: WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3 (Contrast, Minimum, Level AA) requires 4.5:1 for normal text.

bugs.title: Footer links and copyright text fail contrast: grey #676767 on black (3.7:1)
bugs.technique: Accessibility Testing, Colour Contrast Testing
bugs.description: The footer's links (Worldwide, Contact Us, Legal Disclaimer, Cookie Policy, Sitemap, myHyundai) and the copyright line are grey #676767 on black. The measured ratio is 3.71:1, and the text is small.
steps: Open any page on https://hyundai-nishat.com
Scroll to the footer
Check the text and background colours with a contrast checker
bugs.expected: At least 4.5:1 contrast for small footer text.
bugs.actual: 3.71:1 contrast for links and copyright text.
bugs.oracle: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for text smaller than 18 pt (14 pt bold). The footer holds legal links users must be able to read.

bugs.title: The same page is called four different names: "Service Appointment", "Service Appointment Request", "Book a Service" and "Book a Hyundai Service"
bugs.module: Book a Service and Request a Test Drive pages
bugs.technique: Navigation Testing, Content and Spelling Testing, Checklist-Based Testing
bugs.description: The service booking page is "Service Appointment" in the menu, "Service Appointment Request" in the breadcrumb, "Book a Service" as the heading and "Book a Hyundai Service | Online…" in the browser tab. The test-drive page is likewise "Request a Test Drive" on the page but "Book a Hyundai Test Drive" in the tab.
steps: Open After Sales > Service Appointment
Compare the menu item, browser tab title, breadcrumb and page heading
Repeat for Request a Test Drive
bugs.expected: One name per page, used in the menu, tab title, breadcrumb and heading.
bugs.actual: Four names for the service page and two for the test-drive page.
bugs.oracle: Usability heuristic (consistency and standards): users and search engines rely on matching labels to confirm they reached the right page.

bugs.title: "Request a Brochure" has no request form: the page is a plain download list
bugs.technique: Use Case Testing, Navigation Testing, Content and Spelling Testing
bugs.description: The home-page button and page title say "Request a Brochure", which suggests a form where the user asks for a brochure. The page only lists vehicles with Download links. The capitalisation also changes from "Request a Brochure" on the button to "Request a brochure" on the page.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Click "Request a Brochure" in the blue bar under the banner
Look for a form on the page
bugs.expected: Either a request form (as with Request a Test Drive), or a label that matches what the page does, such as "Download a Brochure", with consistent capitalisation.
bugs.actual: No form; only Download links. Button says "Request a Brochure", page says "Request a brochure".
bugs.oracle: Label accuracy: the action name should describe what happens. The sister pages "Request a Test Drive" and Book a Service both contain forms, so users expect one here.

bugs.title: Brochure grid misaligned in two rows (Elantra 1.6 Special Edition and Santa Fe Hybrid)
bugs.technique: Layout and Alignment Testing, Visual Regression Testing, GUI Testing
bugs.description: In row 1 the long name "ELANTRA 1.6 SPECIAL EDITION" wraps and pushes its Download link down (as on the Owner's Manual page, BUG-012). In row 2 the Santa Fe Hybrid image is shorter, so its name and Download link sit higher than the other three.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Click "Request a Brochure" in the blue bar under the banner
Look at the first two rows of vehicles
bugs.expected: All names and Download links in a row line up.
bugs.actual: Row 1: Elantra's Download is lower; row 2: Santa Fe Hybrid's name and Download are higher than the rest.
bugs.oracle: Visual consistency in a grid. The same component misaligns on two pages, which points to a shared template defect.

bugs.title: Owner's Manual downloads (17–76 MB) start immediately, with no file size shown and no preview
bugs.technique: Performance Testing, Volume Testing, Usability Testing, Low Bandwidth / Network Throttling Testing
bugs.description: Clicking Download on the Owner's Manual page downloads the PDF straight away. The files are very large and the page shows no size: Porter H-100 76.4 MB (272 pages), Elantra 1.6 SE 55.1 MB (573 pages), Tucson Hybrid 30.7 MB (754 pages), IONIQ 5 17.0 MB (703 pages). Unlike the brochure links, which open in a browser tab, there is no preview.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Go to After Sales > Owner's Manual
Click Download under ELANTRA 1.6 SPECIAL EDITION
Watch what the browser does
bugs.test_data: Porter_H-100-Owner-Manual.pdf 76,448,008 bytes; Elantra-1_6-SE-Owners-Manual.pdf 55,103,375 bytes; NX4-Hybrid-G1.6T-GDi.pdf 30,702,562 bytes; Ioniq-5-Owner-Manual.pdf 16,995,996 bytes
bugs.expected: The link shows the file type and size (e.g. "PDF, 55 MB") and opens the same way as the brochure links, or offers a preview or chapter-wise download.
bugs.actual: Files of up to 76 MB download at once with no size shown; the brochure page's links behave differently (open in a tab).
bugs.oracle: Usability and performance practice: large downloads should state their size, especially for mobile users on metered data. Consistency oracle: download links on the two pages behave differently.

bugs.title: Elantra and Porter manuals are scanned images: text cannot be searched, selected or read by screen readers
bugs.technique: Accessibility Testing, Static Testing (Reviews), Usability Testing
bugs.description: The Elantra 1.6 SE manual (573 pages) has no text layer at all, and the Porter H-100 manual (272 pages, passed through the free online tool iLovePDF) is almost entirely page images. Ctrl+F finds nothing, text cannot be copied, and screen readers cannot read them.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Go to After Sales > Owner's Manual
Click Download under ELANTRA 1.6 SPECIAL EDITION
Open the downloaded PDF
Press Ctrl+F and search for a word visible on the page, such as "CAUTION"
bugs.expected: A text-based PDF, or one with OCR, so owners can search a 573-page manual for a topic.
bugs.actual: Search finds no results on any page; the file contains only page images.
bugs.oracle: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) and PDF accessibility practice (PDF/UA) require real text. A 573-page reference document that cannot be searched defeats its purpose.

bugs.title: Owner's manuals are generic, dated editions written for left-hand-drive cars (Elantra 2020, IONIQ 5 2022)
bugs.technique: Business Rule Testing, Data Integrity Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The manual's cover does not name any model, its copyright is 2020, and the cover warns that "some models are equipped with Right-Hand Drive (RHD). The explanations and illustrations for some operations in RHD models are opposite of those written in this manual." Cars sold in Pakistan are right-hand drive. The IONIQ 5 manual (created 2022) and Tucson Hybrid manual (2024) carry the same left-hand-drive warning on their covers.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Go to After Sales > Owner's Manual
Click Download under ELANTRA 1.6 SPECIAL EDITION
Open the downloaded PDF
Read the cover page and the Foreword (page F4)
bugs.expected: A manual for the Elantra 1.6 Special Edition as sold in Pakistan: model named, current edition, written for right-hand drive.
bugs.actual: Generic Hyundai manual, "Copyright 2020", no model named, written for left-hand drive with a note that RHD operations are reversed.
bugs.oracle: Data integrity oracle: the link is labelled for a specific 2026 Pakistan model. Pakistan drives on the left with RHD cars, so the manual's instructions and illustrations are mirrored for every local owner.

bugs.title: Tucson Hybrid manual's text layer is corrupted: searching or copying gives gibberish
bugs.technique: Data Integrity Testing, Accessibility Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: The Tucson Hybrid manual (downloaded as NX4-Hybrid-G1.6T-GDi.pdf) shows normal text on screen, but its hidden text layer uses a broken font encoding. Copying "OWNER'S MANUAL" gives "2:1(5Ŕ60$18$/", so Ctrl+F cannot find ordinary words in its 754 pages and screen readers read nonsense.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com
Go to After Sales > Owner's Manual
Click Download under TUCSON HYBRID and open the PDF
Select and copy the text "OWNER'S MANUAL" on the cover page and paste it anywhere, or press Ctrl+F and search for "Maintenance"
bugs.expected: Copied text matches what is on the page; searching for "Maintenance" finds the word.
bugs.actual: Copied text is shifted characters ("Operation" becomes "2SHUDWLRQ"); searching for real words finds nothing.
bugs.oracle: PDF accessibility practice (PDF/UA) and WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 require a text layer that matches the visible text. The other manuals on the same page (e.g. IONIQ 5) extract correctly, so this file is defective.

bugs.title: Content-Security-Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' scripts, weakening protection against XSS
bugs.technique: Security Headers Testing, Security Testing, Vulnerability Scanning, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Testing
bugs.description: The site sends a Content-Security-Policy, but its script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'. These two keywords let inline scripts and eval() run, which removes most of the protection CSP gives against cross-site scripting. securityheaders.com caps the grade because of it. (Found with a passive scan only; no attack was attempted.)
steps: Open https://securityheaders.com
Enter hyundai-nishat.com and click Scan
Read the Warnings section and the Content-Security-Policy raw header
bugs.test_data: Scan of https://hyundai-nishat.com/ on 8 Nov 2026, 13:31 UTC
bugs.expected: script-src limited to 'self' and named hosts, using nonces or hashes for inline scripts, with no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval'.
bugs.actual: script-src 'self' https://www.googletagmanager.com 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; warning: "This policy contains 'unsafe-inline' which is dangerous… 'unsafe-eval' which is dangerous".
bugs.oracle: OWASP Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet and the scanner's own warning: unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval defeat CSP's main purpose. Combined with the weak name and comment validation found on the forms (BUG-013, BUG-026), input handling deserves review.

bugs.title: Server header reveals the exact web server version: "Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)"
bugs.technique: Security Headers Testing, Sensitive Data Exposure Testing, Security Testing
bugs.description: Every response includes "Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)", telling anyone the web server software, its exact version and the operating system.
steps: Open https://securityheaders.com and scan hyundai-nishat.com
Read the Server row in Raw Headers (or check the Network tab in Chrome DevTools)
bugs.expected: A generic Server value (e.g. "Apache") or no Server header.
bugs.actual: Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)
bugs.oracle: OWASP guidance on information leakage (fingerprinting): exact version numbers let attackers look up known vulnerabilities for that version. securityheaders.com flags it under Additional Information.

bugs.title: Second SSL certificate (served to clients without SNI) does not match hyundai-nishat.com and is reported as not trusted
bugs.technique: HTTPS / SSL Testing, Security Testing, Compatibility Testing
bugs.description: The site scores A+ on SSL Labs and its main certificate is valid. However, the server also presents a second certificate, issued only for www.hyundai-nishat.com, to clients that do not send SNI. For the domain hyundai-nishat.com, SSL Labs marks it "Alternative names … MISMATCH" and "Trusted: No, NOT TRUSTED".
steps: Open https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/
Enter hyundai-nishat.com and wait for the report
Scroll to the second certificate and read Alternative names and Trusted
bugs.expected: Every certificate the server can present covers both hyundai-nishat.com and www.hyundai-nishat.com.
bugs.actual: Overall A+, but the second certificate lists only www.hyundai-nishat.com: "MISMATCH" and "NOT TRUSTED" for hyundai-nishat.com.
bugs.oracle: Certificate hostname matching (RFC 6125): a certificate must name the host being visited. Older clients that do not support SNI would see a certificate error instead of the site.

bugs.title: Home page is very slow on mobile: Lighthouse Performance 48, main content appears after 25.1 s
bugs.technique: Performance Testing, Page Load Speed Testing, Low Bandwidth / Network Throttling Testing
bugs.description: In a clean Incognito run (no extensions) on mobile, the home page scores 48/100 for Performance. Largest Contentful Paint (when the main content becomes visible) is 25.1 s and Speed Index 5.8 s; the filmstrip shows a blank white screen for the first several frames. Render-blocking requests add about 1.4 s. An earlier run with extensions scored 38 with LCP 19.3 s, so the problem is consistent.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
bugs.expected: Performance score of 90+ and Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 s (Google's "good" threshold).
bugs.actual: Performance 48; LCP 25.1 s; Speed Index 5.8 s; First Contentful Paint 2.6 s; Total Blocking Time 100 ms.
bugs.oracle: Google Core Web Vitals thresholds: LCP ≤ 2.5 s is good, > 4.0 s is poor. At 25.1 s, ten times the target, mobile visitors wait a long time for the page and many will leave.

bugs.title: Page layout jumps while loading: Cumulative Layout Shift 0.367
bugs.technique: Performance Testing, Visual Regression Testing, Usability Testing
bugs.description: As the home page loads, content moves around: Lighthouse lists "layout shift culprits". Cumulative Layout Shift is 0.367 in both runs, including the clean Incognito run, almost four times the 0.1 limit for a good score.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
bugs.expected: CLS of 0.1 or less, with images and banners given fixed sizes so nothing moves.
bugs.actual: CLS 0.367; Lighthouse flags layout shift culprits.
bugs.oracle: Google Core Web Vitals: CLS ≤ 0.1 is good, > 0.25 is poor. Shifting content makes users tap the wrong element.

bugs.title: Home page downloads 6 MB, with unoptimised images and no long-term caching
bugs.technique: Performance Testing, Volume Testing, Low Bandwidth / Network Throttling Testing
bugs.description: Lighthouse reports a total network payload of 6,091 KiB. It estimates savings of 3,233 KiB from better image delivery, 3,858 KiB from proper cache lifetimes, 52 KiB of unused CSS, 29 KiB of unused JavaScript and 16 KiB of legacy JavaScript. JavaScript execution takes 2.2 s and main-thread work 5.7 s.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
Expand Insights and Diagnostics
bugs.expected: A home page well under 2 MB, images served in modern formats at the right size, and static files cached for a long time.
bugs.actual: 6,091 KiB payload; ~3.2 MB of image savings and ~3.9 MB of caching savings available.
bugs.oracle: Lighthouse "Avoid enormous network payloads" audit and web performance practice; a 6 MB page is costly and slow on Pakistani mobile data connections.

bugs.title: Accessibility audit failures: unnamed dialog, unnamed links, low contrast and skipped heading levels
bugs.technique: Accessibility Testing, Screen Reader Testing, Colour Contrast Testing
bugs.description: Lighthouse Accessibility scores 90 but lists four failed checks: elements with role="dialog" have no accessible name (the booking pop-up), links have no discernible name (icon-only links such as social media), text does not have enough contrast, and headings skip levels.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
Scroll to the Accessibility section
bugs.expected: All four checks pass: dialogs and links have names screen readers can announce, contrast meets 4.5:1, and headings go in order (h1, h2, h3).
bugs.actual: Four failed accessibility checks.
bugs.oracle: WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value), 1.4.3 (Contrast) and 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships). Screen-reader users hear "link" or "dialog" with no description.

bugs.title: Browser errors are logged to the console on the home page
bugs.technique: Error Handling Testing, Grey-Box Testing, Performance Testing
bugs.description: Lighthouse Best Practices (92) fails "Browser errors were logged to the console" and "Issues were logged in the Issues panel in Chrome DevTools".
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
Scroll to Best Practices
Open the Console tab in DevTools to see the errors
bugs.expected: No JavaScript errors or DevTools issues on page load.
bugs.actual: Console errors and DevTools issues are reported.
bugs.oracle: Lighthouse Best Practices audit: console errors point to broken scripts or failed requests that can break features silently.

bugs.title: "Booking your Hyundai?" pop-up covers the home page on every visit, even on mobile
bugs.technique: Usability Testing, Mobile Device Testing, Static Testing (Reviews), Session Management Testing, Cross-Browser Testing
bugs.description: About one second after the home page loads, a large pop-up about booking documents covers the page. In phone view it hides the banner and most of the screen. The page source shows the pop-up (pum-3109) is set to auto-open after 1,000 ms with no cookie, so it returns on every visit even after being closed. Cross-browser check: the same pop-up opens on desktop in Microsoft Edge (ENV-3), covering the middle of the home page.
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in phone view (F12, Ctrl+Shift+M)
Wait one second
Close the pop-up, reload the page
bugs.expected: Booking information shown on the booking page, or a pop-up that appears once and is remembered after the user closes it.
bugs.actual: The pop-up appears on every load and covers most of the mobile screen.
bugs.oracle: Google's guidance on intrusive interstitials (pop-ups that cover the main content on mobile hurt usability and search ranking). Usability heuristic: user control and freedom — a dismissed message should stay dismissed.
bugs.reproducibility: Always (Chrome mobile view and Edge desktop)

bugs.title: SEO audit: links without descriptive text and links search engines cannot crawl
bugs.technique: SEO Testing, Static Testing (Reviews)
bugs.description: Lighthouse SEO scores 85 and fails "Links do not have descriptive text" (1 link found, e.g. generic text such as "Read more") and "Links are not crawlable" (links that use JavaScript or "#" instead of a real address).
steps: Open https://hyundai-nishat.com in Chrome
Press F12 and open the Lighthouse tab
Select Mobile and all four categories, then click Analyze page load
Scroll to the SEO section
bugs.expected: Every link has descriptive text and a real href that search engines can follow.
bugs.actual: Two failed SEO checks.
bugs.oracle: Google Search Central link best practices: crawlable links need an href with a URL, and link text should describe the destination.
